final_answer:
A **stack** follows the **LIFO** (Last-In-First-Out) principle: the most recently added item is the first to be removed. Think of a stack of plates—you take the top plate first.  
A **queue** follows the **FIFO** (First-In-First-Out) principle: the earliest added item is the first to be removed. Imagine a line of people waiting; the first person in line goes next.

**Real-world example for a stack**:  
An **undo/redo** system in text editors. When you make changes (e.g., typing, deleting), each action is added to the undo stack. Pressing “undo” reverts the most recent action, matching LIFO behavior.

**Real-world example for a queue**:  
A **print queue** in an office. Print jobs are added to the queue in the order they’re received. The printer processes them in the same order, ensuring fairness and predictable behavior.
